title: S2 target grouping settle scheduler attribution on current main
discharges: The 2026-08-30 follow-up to isolate the persistent S2 target grouping-apply settle gap before proposing an optimization.

scope.note: Attribution only. The 0.25, 1, and 2 ms cooperative budgets are diagnostic perturbations, not candidate production defaults.

environment.measuredOn: The diagnostic branch at 64e3562c, based directly on unchanged origin/main f7d1808f. The branch adds private bench instrumentation and no production-default change.
environment.cleanBuild: Fresh frozen install, dependency rebuild, and @pretable/app-bench production build in the isolated worktree; Vite preview on 127.0.0.1:4519 with --strictPort.
environment.method: Seven accepted rotated blocks. Each block ran one ordinary target/sort load-fitness control and target/group at 0.25, 1, and 2 ms. Two initial block attempts were rejected wholesale after their sort controls landed outside the established distribution (25.0 ms and 7.8 ms); fresh replacements were used. One separately traced 0.25 ms run is excluded from n=7.
environment.loadFitness: FIT BY CONTROL. Despite a busy shared host early in the sequence, the seven accepted sort controls have a 17.1 ms median and 1.1 ms sample SD, matching the 2026-08-30 control's 17.1 ms / 0.9 ms. Rotation prevents the falling load from being assigned to one budget.

protocol.invariants: All 28 accepted runs completed. All 21 grouping runs reported 50,004 result rows, zero blank-gap frames, zero long tasks, preserved selection/focus, finite non-negative diagnostic fields, an exact top-level phase partition, and a completed query transition.
protocol.standardDeviation: Sample standard deviation (n-1), rounded to 0.1 ms in reported summaries.

control.fitnessVerdict: FIT. The interaction control matches the prior current-main band; the two out-of-band attempts were excluded before analysis.

perturbation.continuity: All budgets kept zero long tasks, zero blank gaps, 50,004 result rows, and preserved selection/focus. The 2 ms max-slice median was 9.9 ms; the largest observed 2 ms slice was 13.1 ms.
perturbation.finding: The perturbation sharply reduces callback count but barely moves scheduler-wait time or the full interval. Yield frequency is measurable, but it is not the dominant source of the persistent gap.

attribution.dominanceRule: A component must have at least 50% median share and lead every completed default-budget run.
attribution.defaultBudgetVerdict: ACTIVE SLICE WORK DOMINATES. It is 77.1% of the full interval at the 0.25 ms production budget and is the largest component in all 7 default-budget runs.
attribution.schedulerWaitVerdict: NOT DOMINANT. Scheduler wait is 14.1% median share. Its count responds strongly to the budget perturbation, but its total time changes only 6.0% from 0.25 to 2 ms.
attribution.reactHandoffVerdict: NOT DOMINANT. Pre-model handoff is 4.6% and post-model surface tail is 2.6% at the default budget.
attribution.residualVerdict: NOT DOMINANT. Unclassified row-model residual is 1.8% at the default budget.

interactionWindow.topFrame: anonymous React package frame at packages/react/dist/index.mjs:14796
interactionWindow.finding: No interaction-window frame explains the full gap, consistent with the measured 4.6% pre-model handoff share.

settleWindow.finding: The dominant slice work is distributed across query evaluation, aggregate/group-tree insertion, persistent structures, and GC. No single sampled frame reaches 10% self time.

comparison.versus2026_08_30: Default-budget settle is 458.3 ms vs 475.3 ms: -17.0 ms (-3.6%), inside the earlier run's 23.0 ms sample SD. The current-main band is unchanged in practical terms.
comparison.versus2026_08_10: Default-budget settle is 458.3 ms vs 401.4 ms: +56.9 ms (+14.2%). The historical gap persists, now attributed primarily to active row-model slice work rather than scheduler waits or React handoff.
comparison.verdict: GAP PERSISTS; ACTIVE SLICE WORK DOMINATES. This pass identifies the component class but does not authorize a production optimization or budget change.

followUps: If optimization is desired, isolate the active-work mix (compiled query evaluation, aggregate/group-index insertion, persistent structures, and GC) in a new design before changing production code.
Do not change the 0.25 ms production budget from this experiment. Any budget proposal must separately rerun the grouped-streaming controls established by the #500 fix arc.
